purpose: Falsifiable hypotheses about the compositional law of small-LLM behavior surfaces. These are theory candidates, not completed results.

hypotheses.statement: For answer-selection behaviors, final-position hidden classifiers tend to become shadows of output or candidate-score geometry unless the task contract prevents the answer interface from already exposing the label.
hypotheses.why_it_matters: It explains why perfect hidden AUC is often a warning sign rather than evidence of a causal mechanism.
hypotheses.current_support: Six atlas rows contain OUTPUT_MARGIN_CONFUND. MC006 repeatedly shows final hidden classifiers matched by candidate-score or final next-token margin. V18 shows the V14 holdout has no margin overlap, V19 improves balance while still failing strict overlap, V20 shows strict final-output overlap is absent even in the pooled V19 bank, V21 shows approximate pair matching still leaves candidate/final margin baselines perfect on holdout, V22 shows source/path monitors remain final-margin-shadowed, V23 shows final next-token margin sign is the greedy binary label boundary, V24 shows delayed JSON city generation breaks the first-token barrier but remains full-completion-candidate-score visible on the selected template, V25 shows candidate-score decoupling can be found but is not enough without shuffled-label robustness, V26 shows locking the V25 coordinate still fails candidate-decoupled template transfer, V27 shows a larger bank can repair source-side candidate decoupling without producing enough transfer-role coverage, V28 shows direct transfer-role repair can find one clean template but not a bank, and the route is now closed as monitor-only.
predicted_next_observations: New final-prompt-token probes on MC006-style factual override tables will keep matching candidate-score or final-output margins.
A final-token hidden result should not be promoted unless the same row split is invisible to candidate scoring and next-token output margins on source-disjoint holdout.
falsifiers: A final-position hidden signature beats candidate-score and final-output baselines by a preregistered margin on a balanced, source-disjoint, behavior-passing table.
The same final-position signature supports a local intervention while matched output/candidate controls fail.
next_tests: Do not treat MC009 as a hidden-state candidate; its first route closed before output/candidate baselines were meaningful.
For the next post-MC009 bridge, report row-position or source-channel baselines, final-output baselines, and candidate-score baselines before hidden-state search.

hypotheses.statement: Earlier hidden signals can predict behavior before same-position output geometry fully exposes it, but such signals should be treated as monitors until an intervention proves they are levers.
hypotheses.why_it_matters: It separates useful pre-decision measurement from causal control and prevents the project from over-promoting lead-time probes.
hypotheses.current_support: MC006 V16 found a pre-output signal that beat same-position output controls, V17 failed additive steering, V18 showed the same table is globally margin-separated on holdout, V19 improved table balance without strict overlap, V20 found only bounded approximate pair-matching inside the V19 bank, V21 showed that approximate pair matching did not neutralize candidate/final margin baselines, V22 mapped source/path and line-boundary monitors that remain final-margin-shadowed, V23 showed the final-margin gate is coupled to greedy generated labels, V24 showed an early hidden monitor still loses to JSON-completion candidate scoring, V25 found a candidate-decoupled hidden monitor that fails shuffled-label selection nulls, V26 showed the locked V25 coordinate fails candidate-decoupled template transfer, V27 showed the expanded candidate-decoupled bank is transfer-insufficient before hidden probing is valid, V28 showed one transfer-ready template is not enough to start hidden probing, and the delayed-city route is closed as monitor-only. MC004 and MC003 found earlier signals that failed robustness controls.
predicted_next_observations: Lead-time signals will be more common than lead-time causal interventions.
Simple additive residual steering at the discovery coordinate will often fail when the downstream decision is distributed across later layers or positions.
falsifiers: A lead-time signal supports a preregistered local intervention that changes generated behavior on holdout while preserving null and side rows.
The same early signal transfers across prompt rewrites and model families without output/candidate controls matching it.
next_tests: Use MC006 delayed-city as a closed monitor-only diagnostic unless a materially different known-confounded causal stress test is preregistered.
Repeat the V22-style lead-time curve on a new row distribution or another behavior family.

hypotheses.statement: Prompt-visible synthetic lookup localizes more readily to source-value attention/write paths than parametric fact override, whose labels become visible through final output and candidate geometry earlier in the audit.
hypotheses.why_it_matters: It defines the bridge needed between MC005 and MC006 instead of pretending synthetic lookup and factual knowledge are the same problem.
hypotheses.current_support: MC005 is now frozen as a bounded source-value mediation surface in layers 24-26: V29 exactly reproduced the direct target source-mask lookup effect with final-query attention-write replacement, while V30-V31 mapped the rare low-to-moderate-margin answer-absent null boundary. MC006 has a behavior substrate and lead-time monitoring signal, but additive control failed, V18 shows the current table is globally margin-separated on holdout, V19's broader prompt bank still fails strict overlap despite better balance, V20 shows strict final-output overlap is absent in that bank, V21 shows approximate pair matching still fails because candidate/final margins perfectly order holdout pairs, V22 shows source/path monitors remain final-margin-shadowed, V23 shows the greedy answer interface itself couples final margin to the parsed binary label, V24 shows delayed city generation can break first-token coupling without beating completion-level candidate scoring on the selected template, V25 shows a candidate-decoupled delayed-city target can still fail shuffled-label hidden-selection nulls, V26 shows the locked V25 coordinate does not transfer to the other candidate-decoupled delayed-city template, V27 shows source-role candidate decoupling is easier than transfer-role coverage in the delayed-city bank, V28 shows transfer-role candidate decoupling is possible but not bank-stable, and the delayed-city route is closed as monitor-only. MC007 V1 shows that familiar entity names can collapse into prompt-local source-value lookup under a terse contract. MC007 V2 shows that explicit authority pressure can create partial real-prior/lure contrast, but parseability and holdout balance fail before hidden-state work is valid. MC007 V3 shows that target-only/compact notes and a stricter answer slot clean the controls but still fail the target-note conflict substrate. MC007 V4 shows that explicit source declarations can decouple from generated city answers and break controls. The V1-V4 route is now closed as a diagnostic bridge rather than a mechanism-promotion path. MC008 V1 now adds a compact symbolic-code bridge diagnostic: generated synthetic lookup and real chemical-symbol recall both pass under the selected symbol_field template, but answer-absent nulls produce UNKNOWN on only 30/40 rows and primary conflicts remain table-dominant with only 8 real-symbol rows, so symbolic code outputs repair direct controls without yet producing a hidden-state-ready bridge. MC008 V2 repaired the symbolic null boundary and preserved direct controls, but the route still closed because primary conflicts were 220 artificial-code rows versus only 2 real-symbol rows. This strengthens the split between prompt-visible lookup and parametric override: compact factual codes remain table-dominated when the prompt contains a matching artificial source value. MC009 removed direct entity-to-code source-value rows and derived the prompt-local answer from row position. The 10-source membership smoke preserved synthetic ordinal lookup, real-symbol memory, and answer-absent null controls at 10/10 each, but failed conflict parseability and real/lure balance. The non-default typed_slot_v2 repair created conflict balance, with 23 derived-code and 19 real-symbol primary rows, but broke synthetic ordinal lookup, broke answer-absent nulls, and exposed the answer channel in the prompt. The first derived-code route is therefore closed as a diagnostic bridge. MC010 then removed both the direct entity-to-code row and the row-position channel with entity-to-handle and handle-to-code indirection. The full 800-row run still failed before hidden-state work: selected neutral_contract had only 23/40 synthetic two-hop task-code rows, only 12/40 real-symbol memory-control rows, and primary conflict was 229 task-code rows versus 0 real/lure-symbol rows despite candidate/output baseline reporting. MC011 changed the answer interface to same-format numeric outputs. This repaired the direct controls completely under the selected neutral_numeric template, with 40/40 synthetic local-number lookup, 40/40 familiar local-number lookup, 40/40 real atomic-number recall, and 40/40 UNKNOWN nulls, but primary conflict still collapsed to 240 local-number rows and 0 atomic/lure-number rows. MC012 changed the source/evaluation contract instead of the answer format. It produced a clean mixed table under compact_reliability, with 40/40 local trusted-source rows and 39/40 atomic untrusted-source rows, but that contrast is prompt-channel visible by design and therefore blocks hidden-state work. MC013 then directly ablated that visible source-status channel. The statused positive control reproduced the MC012 behavior shape, with 40/40 trusted local rows and 39/40 untrusted atomic rows, but the text-identical matched ablation collapsed to 80/80 local-number rows and 0 atomic/lure rows. This shows that under the current numeric prompt contract, the mixed behavior does not survive status-channel removal. MC014 then removed explicit source-status labels and replaced them with calibration rows that had to be checked against standard chemistry. Direct controls and nulls remained clean, and primary prompts had no status lexemes, but the selected conflict table still collapsed to 80/80 local-number rows with 0 atomic/lure rows. This shows that inferred calibration evidence did not overcome prompt-local table dominance under this contract. MC015 then tested a learned-fact parity gate with no visible source-status labels and hidden target/lure atomic numbers. Direct controls and nulls were clean, expected labels were balanced by split, and conflict outputs were mixed rather than fully local, but the outputs did not follow the intended parity rule: selected primary conflict expected correctness was 39/80, expected-local rows selected local 27/40, and expected-atomic rows selected atomic 12/40. This closes parity-gated numeric arbitration as a diagnostic bridge before hidden-state work. MC016 then tested a visible non-status alphabetic gate. Direct controls and nulls were clean, target/lure atomic numbers and source-status lexemes were absent from primary conflict prompts, and expected labels were balanced by split. The selected alphabet_rule template still collapsed to 80/80 local-number primary conflict rows, with expected-local rows selecting local 40/40 and expected-atomic rows selecting atomic 0/40. The stronger feature_labeled_alphabet template also failed to rescue the atomic side, producing 61 local rows, 0 atomic rows, and 19 unparsed rows. This closes visible non-status alphabet gating as another diagnostic bridge before hidden-state work.
predicted_next_observations: A stronger semi-synthetic familiar-entity lookup task should produce a mixture between MC005 and MC006 only after the prompt contract creates real-prior pressure without decoupling declared source from generated city.
Strong parametric priors should shrink the clean source-value write window and increase final-output visibility.
falsifiers: A real-fact override task produces MC005-like local write mediation with strict null reliability.
A familiar-entity synthetic lookup task is fully explained by candidate-score/output geometry despite source-visible artificial values.
next_tests: Do not run MC009, MC010, MC011, MC012, MC013, MC014, MC015, or MC016 hidden-state work from the closed, prompt-visible, ablation-collapsed, calibration-collapsed, parity-failed, or alphabet-collapsed behavior artifacts.

Use a materially different post-MC016 conflict construction that weakens prompt-local table dominance without assigning the answer rule through a visible source-status channel or a simple visible feature channel.
A future bridge must prove rule-aligned learned-fact or operational gating, not merely parseable local outputs, mixed outputs, or visible feature labels.

hypotheses.statement: Under terse table-authoritative contracts, familiar real-world entity names can behave like ordinary lookup keys for artificial prompt-local values, producing no useful real-prior contrast.
hypotheses.why_it_matters: It shows that the MC005-to-MC006 bridge requires controlled prior pressure; familiar names alone are not enough to create a knowledge-conflict substrate.
hypotheses.current_support: MC007 V1 selected the `lookup_only` template, produced 75/80 artificial-value primary rows, 0 real-prior rows, 0 lure rows, and 40/40 UNKNOWN answer-absent null rows. MC007 V2 then showed that explicit numeric authority pressure can create real-prior/lure outputs, so familiar names alone are insufficient but authority framing can move the bridge. MC007 V3 then showed that stricter answer slots and target-only/compact notes do not automatically preserve that contrast. MC007 V4 showed that source labels can be prompt-followed while city answers and controls remain unreliable. The route is closed as diagnostic because ordinary prompt-only repairs did not couple source authority, generated city behavior, parseability, and controls.
predicted_next_observations: Keeping a terse table-authoritative contract will continue to produce artificial-value behavior rather than real-prior conflict.
Adding prior-pressure language without naming the true capital can increase real-prior outputs or reduce artificial-value margins, but the effect will be prompt-contract fragile.
falsifiers: A repeated terse familiar-entity lookup table produces substantial real-prior or lure outputs despite prompt-local artificial values.
Prior-pressure repairs fail to change artificial-value dominance while preserving parseability.
next_tests: Treat V1-V4 as a closed diagnostic route and stop using explicit source labels as city-answer proxies.
Keep the V1 `lookup_only` contract as the clean source-value baseline and the V2 numeric authority dial as the prior-pressure baseline.

hypotheses.statement: Explicit prompt-authority pressure can create artificial-versus-real contrast before the generated-answer table is clean enough for hidden-state work.
hypotheses.why_it_matters: It prevents the project from treating contrast itself as a behavior gate; parseability, holdout balance, and prompt visibility still decide whether a mechanism search is allowed.
hypotheses.current_support: MC007 V2's numeric dial produced 119 artificial, 24 real-prior, 6 lure, and 51 unparsed primary rows. The low-authority numeric panel was the best near miss with 15 artificial and 15 real-prior/lure rows, but parseability was only 75 percent and holdout prior/lure volume stayed weak. MC007 V3 selected the compact-note template, but primary rows were only 55 percent parseable and contained 62 artificial rows versus 4 prior/lure rows; the selected authority-0 panel had 19 artificial, 4 prior/lure, and 17 unparsed rows. MC007 V4 created explicit source/city fields, but selected-template controls failed and source-city consistency was only 47.5 percent on explicit panels and 15.0 percent on conflict panels. The route is now closed as diagnostic: authority pressure can create contrast, but this prompt family cannot produce a clean substrate. MC008 repeats the same pattern in a compact symbolic answer family: stronger authority wording creates a small number of real-symbol conflict rows, but the full selected table is still table-dominant, below 90 percent primary-conflict parseability, and lacks non-holdout/holdout real-or-lure balance. MC008 V2 shows an even sharper authority-pressure boundary: explicit source selection and task-table non-use instructions repaired nulls and parseability, but authority-0 and authority-30 rows each produced only 1/40 real-symbol answers. MC009 changed the authority-pressure test by making the task answer computed from row position rather than copied from a visible entity-code pair. In the 10-source membership smoke, primary conflict rows were 40 derived-code, 7 real-symbol, 0 lure-symbol, and 13 unparsed, so authority pressure still did not produce a clean bridge. The typed_slot_v2 repair produced conflict balance but only by breaking direct controls and exposing the answer channel in the prompt, so the apparent authority contrast is a prompt-visible control artifact rather than a mechanism substrate. MC010 made the prompt-local answer two-hop rather than direct or row-position-derived, but the selected full table still produced 229 task-code primary conflict rows and 0 real/lure-symbol rows. MC011 made the answer format numeric on both sides and kept direct controls clean, but the selected conflict table still produced 240 local-number rows and 0 atomic/lure-number rows. MC012 finally produced a clean authority-driven contrast, with 40 trusted local-number rows and 39 untrusted atomic-number rows, but only through explicit source-status text that is prompt-channel visible by design. MC013 then directly ablated that visible source-status channel. The statused positive control reproduced the MC012 behavior shape, with 40/40 trusted local rows and 39/40 untrusted atomic rows, but the text-identical matched ablation collapsed to 80/80 local-number rows and 0 atomic/lure rows. This shows that under the current numeric prompt contract, the mixed behavior does not survive status-channel removal. MC014 then removed explicit source-status labels and replaced them with calibration rows that had to be checked against standard chemistry. Direct controls and nulls remained clean, and primary prompts had no status lexemes, but the selected conflict table still collapsed to 80/80 local-number rows with 0 atomic/lure rows. This shows that inferred calibration evidence did not overcome prompt-local table dominance under this contract. MC015 then tested a learned-fact parity gate with no visible source-status labels and hidden target/lure atomic numbers. Direct controls and nulls were clean, expected labels were balanced by split, and conflict outputs were mixed rather than fully local, but the outputs did not follow the intended parity rule: selected primary conflict expected correctness was 39/80, expected-local rows selected local 27/40, and expected-atomic rows selected atomic 12/40. This closes parity-gated numeric arbitration as a diagnostic bridge before hidden-state work. MC016 then tested a visible non-status alphabetic gate. Direct controls and nulls were clean, target/lure atomic numbers and source-status lexemes were absent from primary conflict prompts, and expected labels were balanced by split. The selected alphabet_rule template still collapsed to 80/80 local-number primary conflict rows, with expected-local rows selecting local 40/40 and expected-atomic rows selecting atomic 0/40. The stronger feature_labeled_alphabet template also failed to rescue the atomic side, producing 61 local rows, 0 atomic rows, and 19 unparsed rows. This closes visible non-status alphabet gating as another diagnostic bridge before hidden-state work.
predicted_next_observations: Answer-slot-only repairs will continue to trade off parseability, artificial prompt-local dominance, and prior/lure contrast.
Source-label repairs will overstate behavioral clarity unless the city field and controls are audited separately.
falsifiers: A parseability repair eliminates real-prior/lure contrast despite preserving the low-authority real-world question.
A future authority-pressure prompt produces a clean balanced substrate with no prompt-format or candidate-margin visibility.
next_tests: For the next bridge, preserve MC012-level direct controls and conflict mixture while making the answer rule independent of visible trusted/untrusted source-status text, proving that outputs follow the intended rule, and showing that expected-atomic rows survive prompt-local table pressure.

Do not treat calibration-inferred source validity, parity-gated numeric arbitration, or alphabet-gated numeric arbitration as rescue routes unless a new prompt contract first shows learned-fact rows survive against prompt-local table dominance and rule-following failure.

hypotheses.statement: Coarse source-token ablations can show real behavioral dependence while overstating internal circuit locality because source removal and prompt-state recomputation may reproduce most of the effect.
hypotheses.why_it_matters: It keeps source-dependence evidence useful without letting it become a false localized mechanism claim.
hypotheses.current_support: MC001 V9 source masking produced strong behavior movement, but V10/V11 failed compact localization and V12/V13 showed literal rewrites and token/layout controls explain much of the coarse effect.
predicted_next_observations: Future source-token masking successes will often shrink under query-only, head/layer-local, or prompt-rewrite-equivalent controls.
Prompt rewrites will frequently match coarse mask effects when the intervention changes the prompt state rather than a specific generation-time path.
falsifiers: A source-token ablation effect remains large under query-only path intervention, survives rewrite-equivalence controls, and localizes to a small path.
Literal source deletion or neutralization fails to reproduce the coarse mask effect on matched rows.
next_tests: Require source deletion, neutral rewrite, and query-only path comparisons in every source-token control-surface claim.
Add source-rewrite-equivalence fields to future atlas rows.

hypotheses.statement: For the most mechanism-like surfaces, the primary behavior effect can be easier to establish than null locality; rare low-margin null flips define the real boundary.
hypotheses.why_it_matters: It explains why MC005 is valuable without being fully promoted and makes null failures an atlas measurement rather than an annoyance.
hypotheses.current_support: MC005 V29-V31 reproduce the high-margin lookup write effect while answer-absent null rows flip rarely at low-to-moderate margins. The strict 0.5-margin explanation failed, so MC005 is frozen as a bounded mechanism card rather than a promoted card. MC008 extends the null-bottleneck pattern beyond MC005: even with clean synthetic lookup and clean real-symbol memory control, answer-absent symbolic-code rows were 40/40 parseable but only 30/40 UNKNOWN, with 10 other symbol-code outputs. MC008 V2 also shows that not all null boundaries are intrinsic: the V1 symbolic null failure was repaired to 40/40 UNKNOWN by a membership contract, while the conflict boundary remained blocked. MC009 carries this split forward: the selected membership template had answer-absent null rows 10/10 parseable and 10/10 UNKNOWN while conflict parseability and real/lure balance failed; the typed_slot_v2 repair improved conflict balance but collapsed nulls to 0/10 UNKNOWN. Null reliability and conflict balance can therefore trade off rather than improve together.
predicted_next_observations: New MC005 write-replacement variants will preserve lookup effects more easily than they repair answer-absent null locality.
Null flips will cluster near low-to-moderate target/distractor margins rather than across all null rows.
falsifiers: A materially different intervention preserves the lookup effect and eliminates answer-absent null flips under preregistered margin strata.
Fresh null flips appear across high-margin null rows at rates inconsistent with the low-to-moderate-margin boundary.
next_tests: Carry the MC008/MC009 null lesson forward as a required gate: absent rows must stay at least 90 percent UNKNOWN when conflict balance is repaired.
Classify null failure separately from conflict-balance failure so a prompt repair that improves one by breaking the other is killed early.

hypotheses.statement: Hidden-state and intervention work should be blocked until the behavior substrate is parseable, balanced, source-clean, and volume-sufficient.
hypotheses.why_it_matters: Most false mechanism claims can be killed before probing by refusing weak labels.
hypotheses.current_support: MC002 and MC002B never reached valid hidden-state work. MC006 only became useful after V14 repaired a generated-answer behavior table that earlier versions failed. MC007 V1 passed source-value behavior but correctly blocks hidden-state work because the artificial-versus-real contrast is absent. MC007 V2 created contrast but still blocks hidden-state work because parseability and holdout balance fail. MC007 V3 confirms the block: stricter answer-slot prompting cleaned controls while leaving the target-note conflict table too unparseable and imbalanced for probing. MC007 V4 confirms that explicit source labels are not enough when generated city behavior and controls fail. The current MC007 route is closed because all hidden-state prerequisites remain blocked after the ordinary repairs. MC008 V1 is an example of a tempting failed substrate: compact codes clean up synthetic lookup and real-symbol recall, but the behavior gate blocks hidden-state work because null reliability, conflict parseability, and source-disjoint real/lure balance fail. MC008 V2 demonstrates why the behavior gate is multi-axis: even after null, synthetic lookup, real recall, and parseability passed, hidden-state work remained blocked because source-disjoint real/lure conflict balance failed. MC009 then shows why one cannot repair only the failed axis: the membership smoke validated direct controls but failed conflict balance, while typed_slot_v2 repaired conflict balance by breaking synthetic lookup, breaking nulls, and exposing the source channel. MC010 shows the same discipline on the next bridge family: a full 800-row two-hop table with output/candidate baselines still blocks hidden-state work because synthetic lookup, real-symbol memory control, and real/lure conflict balance fail. MC011 isolates a cleaner failure: direct controls and nulls all pass at 40/40 under a numeric answer interface, but hidden-state work is still blocked because the conflict table has 240 local-number rows and 0 atomic/lure-number rows. MC012 shows that passing behavior gates are still not enough: direct controls, nulls, conflict balance, and candidate/output baselines all pass, but hidden-state work remains blocked because the source-status channel is visible by design. MC013 then directly ablated that visible source-status channel. The statused positive control reproduced the MC012 behavior shape, with 40/40 trusted local rows and 39/40 untrusted atomic rows, but the text-identical matched ablation collapsed to 80/80 local-number rows and 0 atomic/lure rows. This shows that under the current numeric prompt contract, the mixed behavior does not survive status-channel removal. MC014 then removed explicit source-status labels and replaced them with calibration rows that had to be checked against standard chemistry. Direct controls and nulls remained clean, and primary prompts had no status lexemes, but the selected conflict table still collapsed to 80/80 local-number rows with 0 atomic/lure rows. This shows that inferred calibration evidence did not overcome prompt-local table dominance under this contract. MC015 then tested a learned-fact parity gate with no visible source-status labels and hidden target/lure atomic numbers. Direct controls and nulls were clean, expected labels were balanced by split, and conflict outputs were mixed rather than fully local, but the outputs did not follow the intended parity rule: selected primary conflict expected correctness was 39/80, expected-local rows selected local 27/40, and expected-atomic rows selected atomic 12/40. This closes parity-gated numeric arbitration as a diagnostic bridge before hidden-state work. MC016 then tested a visible non-status alphabetic gate. Direct controls and nulls were clean, target/lure atomic numbers and source-status lexemes were absent from primary conflict prompts, and expected labels were balanced by split. The selected alphabet_rule template still collapsed to 80/80 local-number primary conflict rows, with expected-local rows selecting local 40/40 and expected-atomic rows selecting atomic 0/40. The stronger feature_labeled_alphabet template also failed to rescue the atomic side, producing 61 local rows, 0 atomic rows, and 19 unparsed rows. This closes visible non-status alphabet gating as another diagnostic bridge before hidden-state work.
predicted_next_observations: Weak behavior substrates will continue to produce impressive but meaningless hidden-state separations.
Parser, prompt-contract, and balance repairs will change which internal signatures appear.
falsifiers: A hidden-state signature discovered on a weak behavior table survives after the behavior table is repaired and balanced.
The same intervention works across the weak and repaired behavior substrates with identical null and side-effect behavior.
next_tests: Do not run hidden-state work from MC009, MC010, MC011, MC012, MC013, MC014, MC015, or MC016.

For the next bridge, require MC012-level direct controls, conflict balance, nulls, parseability, source-disjoint holdout, candidate/output baselines, and an MC013/MC014/MC015/MC016-style prompt-channel and rule-following audit that does not collapse the learned-fact side.

hypotheses.statement: When a control surface transfers across small-model scale, the primary effect may transfer before strict null reliability does.
hypotheses.why_it_matters: It prevents over-reading a successful primary replication as evidence of full mechanism transfer.
hypotheses.current_support: MC005 Qwen3-0.6B reproduced primary lookup behavior but failed strict answer-absent null reliability.
predicted_next_observations: Other transferred surfaces will first reproduce coarse primary movement, then fail side/null/locality gates.
Model-size comparisons will be more informative when null panels are matched before primary effects are celebrated.
falsifiers: A transferred surface preserves primary effect, null locality, side effects, and prompt-contract robustness on the first matched test.
Transfer failures affect primary effect before null reliability across multiple families.
next_tests: Run any future transfer test with matched null panels and side rows from the start.
Do not mark a surface as transferred unless the atlas row's null_locality and transfer fields both move beyond bounded.
